headline: Mule account army
source: Lok Sabha reply on the I4C suspect registry, Dec 2025
captionHeadline: 24.67 lakh bank accounts in India were flagged as "mules", used to move scam money so it can't be traced.
summary: The government's cyber crime centre (I4C) runs a suspect registry with banks. It says the registry has helped block ₹8,031.56 crore. Many mules are ordinary people who "rent out" an account for a small cut.
forYou: The scammer disappears. The account holder is the one the police find.
cta: Send this to the cousin who got a "₹5,000 a month for your account" offer. Follow @postr.news: File #08 drops next.

slides.label: THE OFFER
slides.body: *"₹5,000 a month. Just let us use your bank account."*
slides.title: A TYPICAL OFFER

slides.label: IT SOUNDS EASY
slides.body: You do nothing. Money comes in. Money goes out. *You keep a cut.*

slides.label: WHAT YOU BECAME
slides.body: A *money mule.* The last link in someone else's scam.

slides.label: HOW IT WORKS
slides.title: Your account, their money
points: A scam victim sends money to your account
It hops through more accounts until it vanishes
Your name is the one left on the trail

slides.label: THE NUMBER
slides.body: *24.67 lakh* accounts. Flagged by the government's cyber crime centre.

slides.label: WHO THEY ARE
slides.title: Mostly ordinary people
slides.body: Often students, gig workers or people who needed a little extra money. Many were told it was a "job". The I4C suspect registry shares these accounts with banks so the money can be frozen.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: The scammer disappears. *The mule takes the fall.*

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: At the other end: the very rich, hiding money in *secret companies abroad.* Until the files leaked.
slides.title: FILE #08

slides.label: FOLLOW THE FILES
slides.title: Never rent your account
slides.body: Send this to the cousin who got an "easy money" job offer.
slides.followLine: FILE #08 DROPS NEXT. FOLLOW SO YOU DON'T MISS IT.

collage.note: Rented for a cut. Left holding the case.

headline: Leaked offshore files
source: Government reply in Lok Sabha, 23 Mar 2026
captionHeadline: ₹14,636 crore of hidden foreign income, taxed after the Panama, Paradise and Pandora leaks.
summary: And under the Black Money Act, the tax department raised ₹4,009.64 crore in FY26 (April to December), with 1,368 assessments and 167 prosecutions filed.
forYou: None of it was found by a raid. It was found because someone leaked the files.
cta: Send this to someone who thinks offshore means safe. Follow @postr.news: File #09 drops next.

slides.body: A law firm in *Panama* that kept the world's secrets. Then someone *leaked* them.
slides.title: THE FIRST LEAK

slides.label: 11.5 MILLION FILES
slides.body: Secret companies. Hidden owners. *Indian names among them.*

slides.label: THEN TWO MORE
slides.body: *Paradise Papers*, 2017. *Pandora Papers*, 2021.

slides.label: HOW IT WORKS
slides.title: How money hides offshore
points: Set up a company in a tax haven
Put someone else's name on it as owner
Move money in, out of sight of tax officers
Bring it back as "investment" years later

slides.label: INDIA'S BILL
slides.body: *₹14,636 crore* of hidden foreign income, taxed after the leaks.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: None of it was found by a raid. It was found because *someone leaked the files.*

slides.label: THE QUESTION
slides.body: How many offshore companies *haven't* leaked yet?

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: You don't need a tax haven. *17,818* companies existed only on paper. *Right here.*
slides.title: FILE #09

slides.label: FOLLOW THE FILES
slides.title: Offshore isn't safe
slides.body: Send this to the friend who says the rich never get caught.
slides.followLine: FILE #09 DROPS NEXT. FOLLOW SO YOU DON'T MISS IT.

headline: Ghost GST firms
source: Government reply in Lok Sabha, Dec 2024
captionHeadline: 17,818 companies that existed only on paper. Between them: ₹35,132 crore of suspected GST tax credit claimed.
summary: That's what tax officers found in a special drive against fake GST registrations from April to October 2024. 69 people were arrested.
forYou: No office. No goods. Just invoices.
cta: Send this to your CA friend. They already know. Follow @postr.news: File #10 drops next.

slides.label: THE ADDRESS
slides.body: A company registered at a shop. A flat. Sometimes *a place that doesn't exist.*
slides.title: ON PAPER

slides.label: THE BUSINESS
slides.body: No office. No staff. No goods. *Just invoices.*

slides.label: THE MONEY
slides.body: Every fake invoice lets someone claim *tax credit* from the government.

slides.label: THE TRICK
slides.title: How a ghost firm makes money
points: Issue invoices for goods that never move
Claim GST tax credit on those invoices
Shut it down before anyone visits

slides.label: THE DRIVE
slides.body: April to October 2024. Officers start checking the addresses. *17,818* firms are fake.

slides.label: THE FACES
slides.title: Some used other people's IDs
slides.body: Fake registrations are often made with borrowed or stolen identity documents. The person named as owner may have no idea a company exists in their name.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: You don't need a Swiss bank. You need *a PAN card* and *a printer.*

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: The last file: an app on your phone, where *the house always wins.*
slides.title: FILE #10

slides.label: FOLLOW THE FILES
slides.title: Ghost companies are real
slides.body: Send this to your CA friend. They already know.
slides.followLine: FILE #10 DROPS NEXT. FOLLOW SO YOU DON'T MISS IT.

headline: Betting app machine
captionHeadline: ₹3.3 crore in cash, plus counting machines, found in raids on illegal betting and "dabba trading" apps.
summary: The Enforcement Directorate says ready-made "white-label" betting apps were handed out with admin rights in return for a share of the profits, and a hawala operator moved the money. All accused are innocent until proven guilty.
forYou: The app doesn't need you to win. It just needs you to keep playing.
cta: Send this to the friend who says "bas ek last bet". Follow @postr.news for Season 2.

slides.label: THE AD
slides.body: *"Win ₹10 lakh today."* On your Instagram. Your Telegram. Your cricket stream.
slides.title: YOU'VE SEEN IT

slides.label: THE APP
slides.body: Looks like a game. Feels like a game. *Isn't a game.*

slides.label: JULY 2025
slides.body: The Enforcement Directorate raids betting and *dabba trading* apps in *Mumbai.*

slides.label: THE MODEL
slides.title: A betting app, franchised
points: A ready-made "white-label" betting app is built once
Copies are handed out with admin control
A hawala operator moves the cash, the ED says

slides.label: THE RAID
slides.body: *₹3.3 crore* in cash. And *counting machines.*

slides.label: DABBA TRADING
slides.title: Fake stock market, real losses
slides.body: Dabba trading means betting on share prices outside the stock exchange. No regulator, no protection, and the money never touches a real market. All accused are innocent until proven guilty.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: With admin rights, the operator *controls the app.* The player controls nothing.

slides.label: THE LESSON
slides.body: The app doesn't need you to win. It needs you to *keep playing.*

slides.label: THAT'S THE FILES
slides.body: 10 files. One pattern. *Follow the money.*
slides.title: SEASON 1

slides.label: FOLLOW THE FILES
slides.title: Bas ek last bet?
slides.body: Send this to the friend who is always on a betting app.
slides.followLine: NEW FILES EVERY WEEK. FOLLOW THE MONEY.
